title: UPSC Prelims
content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the public UPSC Civil Services Preliminary syllabus. Not a capture of past exam questions.

items.stem: The lander of the Chandrayaan-3 mission touched down close to the lunar south pole in August 2023. What name was officially given to the landing site?
items.explanation: ISRO named the Chandrayaan-3 landing site Shiv Shakti Point. Tiranga is the name given to the earlier Chandrayaan-2 impact site, while Vikram is the name of the lander itself, not of the site.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - General Studies Paper I

items.stem: The Aditya-L1 spacecraft is positioned at the first Lagrange point of the Sun and Earth system. Approximately how far is this point from the Earth?
items.explanation: The Sun-Earth L1 point lies roughly 1.5 million km from Earth. The figure of about 150 million km is the average Earth-Sun distance and 384000 km is the average distance to the Moon.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - General Studies Paper I

items.stem: At the 2023 New Delhi summit of the G20, which of the following was admitted as a permanent member of the grouping?
items.explanation: India used its G20 presidency to secure permanent membership for the African Union. The European Union is already a permanent member of the G20, while ASEAN and BRICS were not admitted at that summit.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - General Studies Paper I

items.stem: Article 44 of the Constitution of India lays down a directive principle concerning which of the following?
options: Free and compulsory education for children
Protection of wild life and forests
Uniform Civil Code for the citizens
items.explanation: Article 44 directs the State to secure a Uniform Civil Code for the citizens. Education is dealt with in Article 45, village panchayats in Article 40 and protection of wildlife in Article 48A.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - General Studies Paper I

items.stem: The Constitution One Hundred and Sixth Amendment Act, 2023 makes provision for which of the following?
options: Reservation of one third of seats for women in the Lok Sabha and the State Assemblies
Reservation for economically weaker sections in unaided private educational institutions
A fixed five year tenure for members of the Election Commission of India
A separate quota for candidates born in the home state of a cadre
items.explanation: The One Hundred and Sixth Amendment provides one third reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies. Reservation for economically weaker sections came from the One Hundred and Third Amendment and the Election Commission tenure change from the One Hundred and Fourth Amendment.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - General Studies Paper I

items.stem: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, which replaced the Indian Penal Code of 1860 as the general criminal law of India, came into force on which date?
items.explanation: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, together with the new criminal procedure and evidence laws, took effect on 1 July 2024, replacing the Indian Penal Code that had been in force since 1860.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - General Studies Paper I

items.stem: The Supreme Court of India struck down the electoral bonds scheme in February 2024 chiefly on the ground that it violated which right?
options: The right of banks to keep depositors information secret forever
The right of political parties to receive foreign contributions
The right of voters to know the sources of political funding
The right of the Election Commission to decide taxation policy
items.explanation: The Court held that unlimited anonymous political funding impairs the voters right to information, which is part of freedom of speech and expression under Article 19 one (a). The other options do not reflect the reasoning of the judgment.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - General Studies Paper I

items.stem: The United Nations General Assembly declared 2023 as the International Year of which crop, a proposal that was moved by India?
items.explanation: On India's initiative the UN declared 2023 the International Year of Millets, in recognition of the nutritional value and climate resilience of coarse grains. Rice, maize and cotton were not the subject of that declaration.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - General Studies Paper I

items.stem: Which of the following gases is chiefly responsible for the depletion of the ozone layer over the polar regions?
items.explanation: Chlorofluorocarbons release chlorine atoms in the stratosphere that catalytically destroy ozone molecules, which is why the polar ozone hole forms. Carbon dioxide, methane and nitrous oxide are greenhouse gases rather than the main cause of ozone destruction.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - General Studies Paper I

items.stem: Which of the following rivers flows through the Srisailam and Nagarjuna Sagar reservoirs on its way to the Bay of Bengal?
items.explanation: Both the Srisailam and the Nagarjuna Sagar dams stand on the Krishna river. The Godavari, Kaveri and Narmada do not pass through these two reservoirs, and the Narmada flows westward into the Arabian Sea.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - General Studies Paper I

items.stem: Which deficiency in the human diet causes the disease scurvy?
items.explanation: Scurvy results from a lack of vitamin C, which is needed to synthesise collagen, and it causes bleeding gums and slow wound healing. Deficiency of vitamin A causes night blindness, of vitamin D causes rickets and of vitamin B12 causes pernicious anaemia.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - General Studies Paper I

items.stem: Which Indian state has the longest coastline among the states of India?
items.explanation: Gujarat has the longest state coastline in India because of its indented shape and the Gulf of Kachchh and Gulf of Khambhat. Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra have shorter coastlines.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - General Studies Paper I

items.stem: Adam's Bridge, a chain of limestone shoals between India and Sri Lanka, separates which two water bodies?
options: Palk Strait and Gulf of Mannar
Bay of Bengal and Arabian Sea
Andaman Sea and Bay of Bengal
Red Sea and Gulf of Aden
items.explanation: Adam's Bridge, also called Ram Setu, runs between Pamban Island of India and Mannar Island of Sri Lanka, separating the Palk Strait to its north from the Gulf of Mannar to its south.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - General Studies Paper I

items.stem: The black cotton soils of the Deccan plateau are formed mainly by the weathering of which kind of rock?
items.explanation: The regur or black cotton soil of the Deccan trap is derived from the weathering of basaltic lava flows, and it is clay rich and moisture retaining. River alluvium, desert sand and marble are entirely different sources.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - General Studies Paper I

items.stem: Laterite soils in India are formed chiefly as a result of which process?
options: Deposition of silt by annual river floods
Accumulation of organic matter in cold climates
Intense leaching under high rainfall and high temperature
Volcanic ash fall over the northern plains
items.explanation: Laterite soil forms in areas of heavy rainfall and high temperature, where silica is washed away and iron and aluminium oxides are left behind. Flood deposition makes alluvial soil, cold climates slow decomposition and India has no active volcanoes spreading ash.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - General Studies Paper I

items.stem: Which of the following winds crosses the equator during the Indian summer monsoon and feeds heavy rainfall to the west coast of India?
items.explanation: The Somali Jet, also called the Findlater Jet, crosses the equator near the East African coast and turns toward India, carrying moisture to the west coast. The Polar Easterlies stay in high latitudes, the subtropical westerly jet shifts north of the Himalayas in summer and katabatic winds are downslope gravity winds.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - General Studies Paper I

items.stem: The Tropic of Capricorn does not pass through which of the following continents?
items.explanation: The Tropic of Capricorn at about 23.5 degrees south crosses Africa, Australia and South America but no part of Asia, whose landmass lies entirely north of that latitude.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - General Studies Paper I

items.stem: The Great Bath, a large watertight brick tank, was excavated at which Indus Valley Civilisation site?
items.explanation: The Great Bath was found at Mohenjodaro in present day Sindh. Harappa has yielded granaries and coffins, Lothal has a dockyard and Kalibangan has a fire altar and a ploughed field, but none has the Great Bath.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - General Studies Paper I

items.stem: The Ashokan inscriptions were first deciphered in 1837 by which scholar?
items.explanation: James Prinsep deciphered the Brahmi script in 1837 and identified the inscriptions with Emperor Ashoka. Cunningham pioneered the archaeological survey of India, Marshall directed the excavations at Mohenjodaro and Wheeler worked much later in the twentieth century.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - General Studies Paper I

items.stem: The Kalinga war, which is said to have turned Emperor Ashoka toward dhamma and non violence, was fought around which year?
items.explanation: The Kalinga war is generally dated to about 261 BCE, the eighth year of Ashoka's reign, and it was followed by his embrace of Buddhism. 321 BCE marks the foundation of the Maurya empire, 185 BCE its end and 600 BCE belongs to the age of the sixteen mahajanapadas.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - General Studies Paper I

items.stem: The Allahabad Prasasti, which records the military conquests of Samudragupta, was composed by which court poet?
items.explanation: Harisena, the poet at Samudragupta's court, composed the Allahabad pillar inscription. Kalidasa adorned the court of Chandragupta II, Banabhatta wrote during Harsha's reign and Vishakhadatta authored the play Mudrarakshasa.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - General Studies Paper I

items.stem: Which of the following best explains why sound cannot travel through a vacuum?
options: Sound waves are electromagnetic in nature
Sound needs a material medium to propagate
Sound loses all energy in a short distance
Sound travels too slowly to be detected
items.explanation: Sound is a mechanical wave that travels by pushing particles of a medium, so it cannot pass through empty space. Sound waves are not electromagnetic, they do not vanish instantly in a medium and their speed, not their existence, is what varies with the medium.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - General Studies Paper I

items.stem: The revenue settlement known as the zabti or dahsala system is chiefly associated with which minister in the empire of Akbar?
items.explanation: Raja Todar Mal, Akbar's finance minister, organised the zabti or dahsala system of land revenue based on average produce and prices over a cycle of years. Birbal was a courtier, Abul Fazl the historian and Man Singh a general.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - General Studies Paper I

items.stem: Basavanna, the twelfth century figure revered by the Lingayats of Karnataka, is best known for which contribution?
options: Founding the Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition in Bengal
Leading the Alvar devotional movement in Tamil country
Translating the Vedas into Prakrit for the masses
Composing vachana devotional poems in Kannada
items.explanation: Basavanna, minister at Kalyana, spread the Lingayat or Virasasha movement through vachana lyrics in Kannada and encouraged the Anubhava Mantapa. Chaitanya Mahaprabhu founded the Gaudiya tradition, the Alvars were Tamil Vaishnava poet saints and no such Vedic translation is attributed to Basavanna.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - General Studies Paper I

items.stem: The Nehru Report of 1928, drafted by a committee headed by Motilal Nehru, demanded which of the following?
options: Dominion status and a federal constitution with provincial autonomy
Complete independence and immediate withdrawal of British troops
A religious state governed by personal laws of each community
Abolition of all legislatures until the Second World War ended
items.explanation: The Nehru Report of 1928 advocated dominion status, a federal structure and provincial autonomy, and it became the basis of the constitutional demands at the Calcutta session. The other options contradict its moderate constitutional programme.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - General Studies Paper I

items.stem: The Simon Commission, which arrived in India in 1927, was met with nationwide opposition chiefly because
options: it recommended the partition of India
it had no Indian member to represent Indian views
it was sent to impose direct colonial rule
it proposed higher land taxes on farmers
items.explanation: The Simon Commission was an all white body with no Indian member, which is why it was greeted with boycotts and the slogan Simon Go Back. It did not recommend partition, nor was it sent to impose direct rule or raise taxes.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - General Studies Paper I

items.stem: The Karachi session of the Indian National Congress in 1931 is best remembered for adopting a resolution on which subject?
options: The partition of India along communal lines
Recognition of the Muslim League as the sole representative of Muslims
Fundamental rights and the national economic programme
Permanent boycott of all future Round Table Conferences
items.explanation: At Karachi in 1931 the Congress passed a landmark resolution sketching fundamental rights and a national economic programme while ratifying the Gandhi-Irwin Pact. Partition was never adopted by the Congress and Gandhi did attend the second Round Table Conference.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - General Studies Paper I

items.stem: The Quit India resolution was adopted by the All India Congress Committee on which date?
items.explanation: The AICC passed the Quit India resolution in Bombay on 8 August 1942 and Mahatma Gandhi gave the call to do or die. 26 January 1930 is the Purna Swaraj day, 12 March 1930 the start of the Dandi March and 15 August 1947 independence.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - General Studies Paper I

items.stem: Which plan of 1946 proposed a three tier structure consisting of a Union government, groups of provinces and the provinces themselves?
items.explanation: The Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946 proposed groups of provinces under a weak central Union. The Cripps Proposal of 1942 offered dominion status after the war, the Wavell Plan of 1945 concerned an interim government and the Simon Commission Report of 1930 dealt with provincial autonomy.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - General Studies Paper I

items.stem: The directive principle concerning a Uniform Civil Code for the citizens, contained in Article 44, has been borrowed from the constitution of which country?
items.explanation: The Directive Principles of State Policy were borrowed from the Irish Constitution, which had itself drawn on the Spanish constitution. Fundamental Rights came from the United States and the idea of a federation with a strong centre from Canada.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - General Studies Paper I

items.stem: Dr B R Ambedkar described which article of the Constitution as the heart and soul of the Constitution?
items.explanation: Article 32 empowers the Supreme Court to issue writs for the enforcement of fundamental rights, and Ambedkar called it the heart and soul of the Constitution because it makes the other rights effective. Articles 19, 21 and 14 grant freedoms, life and equality but do not provide the remedy itself.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - General Studies Paper I

items.stem: The power of the President of India to promulgate ordinances when Parliament is not in session rests on which article of the Constitution?
items.explanation: Article 123 empowers the President to promulgate ordinances, and the corresponding power of the Governor is in Article 213. Article 143 deals with the advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court, Article 110 with money bills and Article 280 with the Finance Commission.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - General Studies Paper I

items.stem: The Constitution Seventy Third Amendment Act, 1993 gave constitutional status to which institutions?
options: River valley authorities for interstate rivers
items.explanation: The Seventy Third Amendment inserted Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule, creating a three tier Panchayati Raj system with elections and reservations. Urban local bodies were covered by the Seventy Fourth Amendment, and the other options are not its subject.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - General Studies Paper I

items.stem: What is the maximum permissible strength of the Rajya Sabha as fixed by the Constitution of India?
items.explanation: Article 80 caps the Rajya Sabha at 250, comprising up to 238 elected representatives of states and union territories and 12 members nominated by the President. 245 is the present strength and 545 or 552 are figures associated with the Lok Sabha.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - General Studies Paper I

items.stem: Which article of the Constitution provides for the Finance Commission to be constituted by the President at intervals of five years?
items.explanation: Article 280 provides for a Finance Commission appointed by the President every five years to recommend the distribution of taxes between the Union and the states. The other articles deal with the effect of the Commissions recommendations and borrowing and guarantees.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - General Studies Paper I

items.stem: The Monetary Policy Committee of the Reserve Bank of India is mandated to keep the retail inflation rate near which target?
options: Six percent with no tolerance band
Two percent with a tolerance band of plus or minus one percent
Three percent with a tolerance band of plus or minus three percent
Four percent with a tolerance band of plus or minus two percent
items.explanation: The amended RBI Act, 1935 sets the consumer price inflation target at four percent with a band of two percentage points on either side, to be reviewed every five years. The other figures do not appear in the inflation targeting framework.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - General Studies Paper I

items.stem: NITI Aayog, which replaced the Planning Commission of India, came into existence on which date?
items.explanation: NITI Aayog was constituted by executive resolution on 1 January 2015 in place of the Planning Commission that had been set up in 1950. The other dates do not correspond to its establishment.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - General Studies Paper I

items.stem: The Goods and Services Tax Council, which is a constitutional body, has been created under which article of the Constitution?
items.explanation: Article 279A inserted by the Constitution One Hundred and First Amendment Act, 2016 creates the GST Council. Article 246A deals with the legislative power to make laws on GST and the other articles with apportionment and restrictions on taxation.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - General Studies Paper I

items.stem: The Ramsar Convention, the intergovernmental treaty for the conservation and wise use of wetlands, was adopted in which year and place?
options: 1992 at Rio de Janeiro in Brazil
1945 at San Francisco in the United States
items.explanation: The Convention on Wetlands was adopted at Ramsar, Iran in 1971. The 1972 Stockholm conference dealt with the human environment, the 1992 Rio conference with sustainable development and biodiversity and the 1945 San Francisco meeting founded the United Nations.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - General Studies Paper I

items.stem: Project Tiger, the centrally sponsored conservation programme, was launched in April 1973 from which national park?
items.explanation: Project Tiger began on 1 April 1973 with the Jim Corbett National Park as its first reserve and nine reserves in the first year. Kaziranga is known for the rhinoceros, Periyar for elephants and Sariska lies in Rajasthan, but none is the launch site.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - General Studies Paper I

items.stem: Read the following passage. A district administration found that young people were leaving the village even though the harvest had been good for three years running. Investigation showed that work after sowing was short and that families preferred the certainty of a monthly wage in the town to the uncertain earnings of daily farm labour. According to the passage, why did migration continue despite good harvests?
options: Farm work offered only short and uncertain employment
The villagers disliked farming as a matter of principle
The town was nearer to the village than the fields were
Government rules compelled the youths to leave
items.explanation: The passage states that work after sowing was short and that families chose the certainty of a monthly wage over uncertain daily farm earnings, so employment uncertainty rather than crop failure explains the migration.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - CSAT Paper II

items.stem: Continuing with the passage about villagers leaving despite good harvests, the district decided to widen the MGNREGA guarantee so that it covered the lean months. Which assumption underlies this decision?
options: Farmers refuse to work during the harvest season
Work during the lean months would reduce distress migration
Monthly wages are always lower than farm earnings
The harvests will fail in the coming year
items.explanation: If the lean months provide guaranteed wages, families will not need to migrate for security, so the decision assumes that lean season work reduces distress migration. The other options contradict the facts given in the passage.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - CSAT Paper II

items.stem: In the passage about migration from a village whose harvests were good, what is the writer's attitude toward the migrating youths?
options: Angry that the youths abandon their families
Indifferent to whether they stay or leave
Sympathetic and explanatory rather than disapproving
Convinced that the town offers them a worse life
items.explanation: The writer explains the economic motives of the migrants and presents the district response as a solution, which shows an understanding rather than blame. The passage expresses no anger, indifference or judgement that town life is worse.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - CSAT Paper II

items.stem: Read the following passage. Installing computers in a school does not by itself improve learning. Teachers who are not trained to use the machines tend to revert to lecturing, and students use the same machines for games in the evening. Reformers therefore argue that money spent on equipment without spending on teacher training is wasted, while administrators reply that the equipment at least familiarises children with technology. What is the main claim of the reformers in this passage?
options: Computers should be removed from every school
Students learn more from games than from teachers
Administrators do not care about examination results
Investment in equipment alone cannot improve learning
items.explanation: The reformers argue that equipment bought without teacher training produces no learning gain, which is precisely the claim that spending on hardware alone is wasted. The passage never says computers should be removed or that games educate better.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - CSAT Paper II

items.stem: In the passage on computers in schools, the administrators reply that the equipment at least familiarises children with technology. This reply implicitly assumes that
options: Even limited exposure to technology has value for students
Familiarity with technology automatically raises examination scores
Teacher training is unnecessary in modern schools
Students always prefer machines to teachers
items.explanation: The word at least shows the administrators are claiming a modest benefit from mere exposure, so their assumption is that some familiarity with technology is worthwhile in itself. The stronger claims are not stated or supported.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - CSAT Paper II

items.stem: Which of the following best states the lesson that the passage on computers in schools is intended to convey?
options: Schools should buy computers only after examinations
Hardware and teacher capacity must be funded together
Technology reduces the need for teachers
Games are an essential part of the school curriculum
items.explanation: The passage contrasts equipment with training and shows that each fails without the other, so the lesson is to fund hardware and teacher capacity together. The remaining options go against the passage.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - CSAT Paper II

items.stem: Find the missing number in the series 4, 9, 19, 39, 79, ?
items.explanation: Each term is obtained by doubling the previous term and adding one, since 4 into 2 plus 1 is 9, 9 into 2 plus 1 is 19 and so on. Applying the rule to 79 gives 159, so the other choices are wrong.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - CSAT Paper II

items.stem: Find the missing number in the series 3, 8, 18, 38, 78, ?
items.explanation: Here every term equals twice the previous term plus two, because 3 into 2 plus 2 is 8 and 8 into 2 plus 2 is 18. Continuing the pattern, 78 into 2 plus 2 gives 158.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - CSAT Paper II

items.stem: In a certain code each letter of a word is written as the letter that comes one place after it in the alphabet, so that MONKEY becomes NPOLFZ. How will CHAIR be written in that code?
items.explanation: Shifting each letter of CHAIR one place forward gives D, I, B, J and S, so the code is DIBJS. The other choices misplace at least one letter of the shift.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - CSAT Paper II

items.stem: Pointing to a photograph, a man said that she is the daughter of the only son of my grandfather. How is the woman in the photograph related to the man?
items.explanation: The only son of the man's grandfather is the man's father, and the daughter of his father is his sister. She therefore cannot be his mother, aunt or niece.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - CSAT Paper II

items.stem: Ravi walks five kilometres towards the north, turns right and walks three kilometres, then turns right again and walks five kilometres. In which direction is he now with respect to his starting point?
items.explanation: A right turn from north faces east and a right turn from east faces south, so after walking east by three kilometres and then south by five he ends up three kilometres due east of the start.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - CSAT Paper II

items.stem: Statements. Some pens are books and all books are rulers. Conclusions. I. Some pens are rulers. II. Some rulers are pens. Which of the following is correct?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
items.explanation: From some pens are books and all books are rulers it follows that some pens are rulers, and converting that particular proposition gives some rulers are pens, so both conclusions are valid.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - CSAT Paper II

items.stem: A company decided to pay a festival bonus to all of its employees before Diwali. Which of the following is an implicit assumption behind this decision?
options: Employees need extra money during the festival season
The company had recorded a loss in the previous year
Festival bonuses are compulsory under the income tax law
Employees will refuse to work after the festival
items.explanation: A bonus timed with the festival presupposes that employees have higher expenses and value extra money at that time. Loss, legal compulsion and threats of refusal are neither stated nor needed for the decision.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - CSAT Paper II

items.stem: Assertion A. The melting of floating sea ice does not raise the global sea level. Reason R. Floating ice already displaces a volume of water equal to the weight of the ice. Which of the following is correct?
options: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
items.explanation: By Archimedes principle floating ice displaces water equal to its own weight, so when it melts the resulting water occupies the same volume and the sea level does not change. Both statements are therefore true and the reason explains the assertion.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - CSAT Paper II

items.stem: A wayside station has a single platform. A mail train is running two hours late, an express train is on time and a passenger train is carrying patients to a district hospital. Which order of entry should the station master adopt?
options: The late mail train first because it is already behind schedule
The express train first because it is running on time
The patient carrying passenger train first, then the express and then the mail train
Hold every train until the delayed mail train passes
items.explanation: The urgency of getting patients to hospital outweighs schedule considerations, after which the punctual express should be cleared and the already delayed mail train can wait longest. Prioritising lateness or punctuality ignores the human emergency.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - CSAT Paper II

items.stem: A country produced 1200, 1100, 1400 and 1550 tonnes of a commodity in 2019, 2020, 2021 and 2022 respectively, while its imports were 300, 420, 380 and 500 tonnes in those years. In which year was production minus imports the highest?
items.explanation: The differences are 900 in 2019, 680 in 2020, 1020 in 2021 and 1050 in 2022, so 2022 gives the largest surplus of domestic production over imports.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - CSAT Paper II

items.stem: Imports of a commodity rose from 300 tonnes in 2019 to 500 tonnes in 2022 while domestic production rose from 1200 to 1550 tonnes in the same period. The percentage increase in imports over these years was approximately
items.explanation: The rise in imports is 200 tonnes on a base of 300, and 200 divided by 300 multiplied by 100 gives about 66.7 percent. Production rose by only about 29 percent, so the other options do not match the import change.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - CSAT Paper II

items.stem: The price of sugar rises by 25 percent. By what percentage must a household reduce its consumption of sugar so that its total expenditure on sugar does not increase?
items.explanation: If the original price is 100 the new price is 125, so the same expenditure buys only 80 units, which is a fall of 20 percent from 100. A cut of 25 percent would overspend and the other figures do not restore the original total.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - CSAT Paper II

items.stem: A train 180 metres long passes a pole standing beside the track in 12 seconds. What is the speed of the train in kilometres per hour?
items.explanation: Covering 180 metres in 12 seconds gives 15 metres per second, and multiplying by 3.6 converts that to 54 kilometres per hour, so the other choices correspond to incorrect conversions.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - CSAT Paper II

items.stem: The average of five numbers is 42. If one of the numbers, which is 50, is removed, what is the average of the remaining four numbers?
items.explanation: The total of the five numbers is 5 times 42 which is 210, and removing 50 leaves 160. Dividing 160 by 4 gives an average of 40 for the remaining numbers.
items.reference: UPSC Prelims Syllabus - CSAT Paper II
